learningObjectives: Explain salience as behavioural relevance rather than threat alone.
Describe the proposed role of network switching.
Connect interoception and clinical symptoms cautiously.

anatomy.label: Anterior insula
anatomy.detail: Anterior insular regions integrate interoceptive, affective and cognitive information.
anatomy.clinical: Relevant to panic, pain, craving and awareness of internal state.

anatomy.label: Dorsal anterior cingulate
anatomy.detail: Dorsal cingulate regions participate in effort, conflict, autonomic coordination and action selection.
anatomy.clinical: Persistent recruitment may accompany high control demand or threat monitoring.

anatomy.label: Limbic interactions
anatomy.detail: Salience systems interact with amygdala and other subcortical structures to shape relevance.
anatomy.clinical: Salience should not be reduced to the amygdala or fear.

anatomy.label: Interoceptive pathways
anatomy.detail: Visceral and autonomic inputs inform estimates of bodily condition and urgency.
anatomy.clinical: Misinterpretation of bodily signals can amplify panic or health anxiety.

anatomy.label: Network switching
anatomy.detail: The salience network has been proposed to help shift between default-mode and executive systems.
anatomy.clinical: Switching is a useful model, not a settled single-mechanism explanation.

interaction.title: Salience Network sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow information flow across the network.

stages.label: Sample
stages.text: Monitor external events and internal body signals.

stages.label: Recruit
stages.text: Engage attention, control and autonomic systems.

stages.label: Update
stages.text: Reduce or sustain response as new evidence arrives.

quizBank.question: Salience most closely means:
quizBank.explanation: Salience concerns what matters for current goals or bodily needs.

quizBank.question: A core salience-network region is the:
quizBank.explanation: Anterior insula is commonly identified as a core node.

quizBank.question: Interoception refers to:
options: Sensing the internal condition of the body

quizBank.question: The salience network may help:
options: Coordinate shifts between internal and task-focused systems
quizBank.explanation: It may facilitate switching and recruitment based on relevance.

quizBank.question: A clinically careful interpretation is that salience hyperactivity:
options: May reflect several processes and is not diagnostic by itself
quizBank.explanation: Salience findings are transdiagnostic and context dependent.
